title: fetch() call in XHTML/JS without AbortController signal — hangs when engine is offline
description: Browser-side fetch() calls to a local engine endpoint (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8042) without an AbortController/signal will hang for the browser's default TCP connection timeout (60-120 seconds) when the engine is offline or unreachable. This freezes the UI section waiting on the result and blocks dependent cascade logic. In XHTML-WorkspaceHub.xhtml the engine monitor, test actions and scan cascade all use fetch() calls that should fail fast (5-10s). Without a timeout signal, the user sees a spinner for 60-120s before any fallback logic runs. This is especially important in file:// opened XHTML pages where no server-side timeout exists.
ps_version_scope_note: JavaScript-side pattern. Applies to all XHTML and HTML files containing fetch() to local engine endpoints.
detection_method: Scan XHTML/HTML/JS files for fetch( calls to local engine base URLs without AbortController or signal: or AbortSignal.timeout
remedy: Add AbortController wrapper to all fetch() calls that target LOCAL_ENGINE_BASE or ENGINE_BASE URLs. Set a timeout of 5000-10000ms. Update the scan/test cascade functions to abort and fall through to the next cascade mode on timeout.

known_instances.risk: MEDIUM — 60s hang per fetch when engine offline
